// diagnostic

E3401

`{pure_fn}` calls the impure function `{call}`.

What

`{pure_fn}` calls the impure function `{call}`.

Why

A `fn … -[]>` may only call other `fn … -[]>`s and pure builtins. Impure calls make the result non-deterministic (D-PURE2). In `jet eval --pure` the whole call graph from `run` is checked transitively; the why-line shows the full chain (`run → a → b calls \`print\``) so the user can find the leak. Compile-time (`@` blocks, `@name :: expr` bindings) shares this same call-graph walk (D-META-EFFECT1 c3): the message reads `{call}` is not allowed in comptime code instead, since there is no enclosing `-[]>` function name to report.

Fix

Mark `{call}` as `fn … -[]>`, or remove the call from `{pure_fn}`; at compile time, compute the value at runtime instead.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E3401: tests/ui/comptime_impure.stderr.

Error [E3401]: `print` is not allowed in comptime code
  --> tests/ui/comptime_impure.jet:2:5
    |
  2 |     print("side effect")
    |     ^^^^^
 Why: build calls `print`, which touches the outside world — comptime must give the same answer on every machine
 Fix: compute this at runtime instead; the exceptions are `embed_file("path")`, `embed_bytes("path")`, and `find("glob")`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3401

Error [E0107]: nothing named `@x` exists here
  --> tests/ui/comptime_impure.jet:8:20
    |
  8 | fn run() { print("{@x}") }
    |                    ^^
 Why: a name must be declared before it's used
 Fix: declare it first: `@x :: ...`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0107
